Siding Services in St. Louis, MO
Siding Services in St. Louis, MO - Strong Protection for Every Season

Your siding is the first shield between your home and the weather. In St. Louis, that means standing up to sticky summer heat fed by the Mississippi and Missouri rivers, hail from spring storms, and winter freeze-thaw cycles that crack weak panels. When siding fails, water seeps into your wall cavities. That leads to mold, wood rot, and damage that costs far more to fix than the siding itself.

Coldstream Exteriors handles full-service siding installation , siding repair , and siding replacement for homeowners across St. Louis and nearby towns. We use materials built for local weather, and we back every job with clear pricing and honest timelines.
Call Coldstream Exteriors at (314) 380-8111 today to schedule your siding services in St. Louis, MO .
Your Trusted Local Siding Contractor in St. Louis

Siding damage is not always easy to spot from the curb. Small cracks near window trim, paint that bubbles, or soft spots along the base of your panels can mean water is trapped behind the surface. Left alone, these issues grow. Mold spreads inside walls. The padding breaks down. Heating and cooling costs go up.

A skilled siding contractor catches these issues early. At Coldstream Exteriors, we check the full outside of your home before we suggest any work. We look at your panels, the layer beneath them, the flashing, and your soffit and fascia . If only a small section needs work, we fix that section. If a full swap makes more sense, we tell you why and walk you through your choices.
We also work with our roofing , window , and gutter teams when your project covers more than siding. That keeps your timeline short and avoids gaps between trades.
What to Expect During Your Siding Project
Every siding job starts with a close look at your home. Here is how the process works from start to finish:
On-site check: We look at your current siding, measure the outside of your home, and find any water damage, rot, or padding issues behind the panels.
Material choice: We help you pick between options like vinyl siding and fiber cement siding based on your budget, home style, and weather needs.
Prep and removal: Our crew takes off old siding with care, checks the boards beneath, and fixes any damaged areas before new panels go up.
Install: We put up your new siding to the maker's specs, seal all joints and flashing, and make sure every panel sits level and tight.
Final walkthrough: We clean the job site, go over the finished work with you, and make sure you are happy before we wrap up.
Our Siding Services in St. Louis
We offer a full range of home siding services built around the needs of St. Louis homeowners:
Siding Installation : New siding for new builds or homes that need a full exterior upgrade. We handle material sourcing, prep, and install.
Siding Replacement : Full removal and swap of old, failing, or storm-hit siding. Includes board checks and repair as needed.
Siding Repair : Targeted fixes for cracked, loose, or warped panels. Great when damage is limited to one area of your home.
Vinyl Siding : A budget-friendly, low-care option that fights moisture and holds up well in humid spots like St. Louis.
Fiber Cement Siding : A strong, long-lasting option built to handle hail, high winds, and big temperature swings. It resists rot, fire, and pests.
Soffit and Fascia Services : Repair or swap of the panels that guard your roofline and vent your attic. Damaged soffit and fascia invite pests and trap moisture.
Common Siding Problems We Fix in St. Louis
St. Louis weather puts steady stress on your home's outer shell. These are the issues we see most often:
Cracked or split panels: Freeze-thaw cycles through St. Louis winters cause vinyl and wood siding to crack. North-facing walls with less sun take the worst hits.
Warping and buckling: Summer heat above 90°F paired with river-fed humidity makes panels expand and shift. Poorly hung siding warps faster.
Water behind siding: Failed caulk around windows, vents, or trim lets rain seep behind panels. Over time, this leads to mold and rotted boards.
Fading and chalking: UV rays bleach color from older siding. A chalky film on the surface means the material is wearing out.
Storm and hail hits: St. Louis sits in a busy severe weather zone. Hail dents vinyl, cracks fiber cement, and chips paint off wood siding. Wind gusts above 60 mph rip panels loose.
Pest entry points: Gaps in damaged siding give bugs and rodents a straight path into your walls. Carpenter bees and wasps target rotted wood siding the most.
If you see any of these signs, reach out for a free check. Catching issues early stops water damage from spreading deeper into your home.

Frequently Asked Questions About Siding in St. Louis
How much does siding installation cost in St. Louis?

Most St. Louis siding installations range from $8,500 to $25,000, depending on your home's size and material choice. A typical 2,000 square foot home with vinyl siding averages $9,000-$14,000. James Hardie fiber cement typically costs $15,000-$25,000. We provide detailed written estimates after your free consultation, and you pay nothing until installation is 100% complete.
How long does siding installation take in St. Louis?

Most residential siding installations take 3-7 days with our experienced crews. Simple ranch homes can often be completed in 2-3 days, while complex two-story homes typically take 5-7 days. New construction timelines coordinate with your builder's schedule. Weather conditions can affect the timeline.
What siding materials do you recommend for St. Louis homes?

Vinyl siding remains popular for St. Louis homes due to its affordability and low maintenance. Fiber cement siding offers superior durability, lasting 30-50 years with proper installation. During your consultation, we show you samples and explain which materials work best for your home and budget.
Do you handle siding installation for new construction projects?

Yes, we work with homeowners, builders, and contractors on new construction siding installation throughout St. Louis. We coordinate with your construction timeline, deliver materials on schedule, and install your siding system according to code requirements and manufacturer specifications.

Building code allows overlay installation in some situations, but we rarely recommend it. Complete removal lets us inspect your sheathing, replace damaged wood, and install new house wrap. This approach delivers better long-term performance and allows full manufacturer warranties.
How do I know if my siding needs repair or full replacement?

If damage hits only a few panels or a small section, repair is usually the better move. When you see cracking, warping, or water damage across more than one wall, full replacement saves more money over time. Our team checks your home and gives you a straight answer.

We handle most preparation, but homeowners should move vehicles out of the driveway, relocate outdoor furniture away from the house, and keep children and pets inside during installation. We'll provide a complete preparation checklist before we start.

Fiber Cement Siding in St. Louis, MO
Professional Fiber Cement Siding Services in St. Louis, Missouri

Your home deserves more than just any exterior covering. Whether you're building new construction, adding a garage, or installing fiber cement siding on your existing home, the quality of that installation determines everything. How long your siding lasts. How well it protects your belongings. How much you spend on energy bills. How your home looks from the street. One professional installation done right protects your family and your investment for decades. One careless installation creates problems you'll fight for years.

When you're ready to install fiber cement siding, you face dozens of decisions that seem overwhelming. Which manufacturer performs well in Missouri's climate? How much clearance does your siding need above grade? What house wrap provides real protection? Should you upgrade your sheathing? These aren't just technical details. They're the difference between siding that performs beautifully for 50 years and panels that fail in year seven.
Why St. Louis Homeowners Need Reliable Fiber Cement Installation

Here's what separates professional fiber cement installation from amateur work. The materials are only half the equation. How those materials get installed matters just as much as which brand you choose. We've removed countless siding systems that used premium fiber cement but failed early because someone rushed the installation, skipped critical steps, or didn't understand proper moisture management.

St. Louis weather demands more from your siding than most people realize. Spring thunderstorms test every panel's impact resistance. Summer heat and humidity stress materials relentlessly. Fall windstorms challenge every fastener's holding power. Winter freeze-thaw cycles push moisture into gaps where poor installation leaves vulnerabilities. Your siding needs to handle all of this, year after year, without compromise.

Picture this common scenario. You hired the lowest bidder to install your new fiber cement siding last year. Everything looked fine when they finished. But now you're noticing problems. Small gaps forming around your windows. Panels cracking where moisture got trapped. Dark streaks where improper flashing let water behind the siding. Your beautiful new exterior is failing, and the company that installed it stopped returning your calls months ago.

Poor installation doesn't announce itself with obvious signs on day one. It reveals itself slowly through premature failure, costly repairs, and frustration. By the time you realize something's wrong, your warranty claims get denied because "improper installation voids coverage." You're stuck paying twice for the same siding.

We specialize in professional siding installation that solves problems before they start. We're not here to rush through your project and move to the next job. We're here to give you properly installed fiber cement with quality materials, experienced crews, and guarantees that actually mean something.

Maybe you're adding a second story and need seamless integration with your existing exterior. Maybe your current siding is beyond repair and needs complete removal and reinstallation.
Whatever brings you here, you probably have questions. What's the best approach for your situation? How long will installation take? What can you expect during the process?
